detail:
Beyond Celiac reports on FB102, an investigational antibody treatment for celiac disease sponsored by argenx. According to the company's preliminary phase 2 report, FB102 protected the small intestine from damage due to gluten consumption in study participants, and participants who received the drug also had changes in symptoms and markers of inflammation. The sponsor plans to advance FB102 into a phase 3 trial, and the drug has received an FDA Fast Track designation, which can speed the agency's review of promising drugs.

Beyond Celiac notes that drug development is slow and uncertain: on average it takes more than 10 years for a drug to move from idea to market, and about 90 percent of drugs never reach the market at all. The organization supported recruitment for the FB102 phase 2 study and expects fuller results to be shared at a future scientific meeting. FB102 remains investigational, and the gluten-free diet remains the only established treatment for celiac disease.

Tabs is not endorsing or verifying this material. Talk to your doctor about celiac disease research and clinical trials.
sourceVideoTitle: Confident in Results, argenx Plans to Move Celiac Drug Forward
summary: Beyond Celiac reports that argenx plans to move its investigational celiac drug FB102 into a phase 3 trial after phase 2 results suggested it protected the small intestine from gluten damage, while the gluten-free diet remains the only established treatment.
takeaways: all drug candidates are investigational and in trials
a phase 3 trial is planned, the last phase before a drug can be sold
most drugs in development never reach the market, the source notes
research participation is optional; talk to your doctor about studies
title: Where celiac disease research is heading
